title: Add tier/deployment_mode tags to SLI metrics at ingress (and propagate through request context)
author: Amara Diallo
description: Context: As part of the Tiered SLO + Error Budget program, we need to compute SLIs (success rate, latency, streaming reliability) separately for Hosted (shared) vs Dedicated (reserved capacity). Today most gateway metrics are emitted without a reliable tier signal, and routing/fallback can further obscure the original customer tier in downstream services. This PR adds tier/deployment mode tags to ingress SLI metrics and ensures the tags are attached to the request context so they can be propagated into routing, traces, and downstream metrics. Summary of changes: (1) Introduce a canonical tier classifier at ingress that maps requests into tier={hosted|dedicated} and deployment_mode={hosted_api|dedicated_pool} (naming aligned with ADR-0142 draft). (2) Add these tags to the gateway SLI metric set for request count, request duration histograms, and streaming termination counters. (3) Propagate tier/deployment_mode via RequestContext (headers -> internal ctx) so routing can preserve tier across fallback/region-shift decisions and telemetry can emit consistent tags. (4) Add guardrails to avoid cardinality explosions: we do NOT add customer_id/model_id labels at ingress; those remain sampled/derived in dedicated dashboards only, behind existing access controls. (5) Provide migration notes for dashboards/recording rules: existing queries using legacy label "pool" or "account_tier" should switch to tier/deployment_mode; a compatibility recording rule is included for a 2-week deprecation window. Details: Metrics affected include api_gateway_request_total, api_gateway_request_duration_seconds_bucket, api_gateway_stream_termination_total, and api_gateway_errors_total. For streaming, we tag the termination reason classification at the gateway boundary (client_abort vs server_disconnect vs upstream_error) using the existing SSE/WebSocket close signals and a small set of heuristics; only server_disconnect and upstream_error count against streaming reliability SLI (client_abort excluded per the SLI spec). Rollout plan: This ships behind config flag telemetry.tier_tagging.enabled (default off). We’ll enable in staging for 48h, then canary 5% prod, then 100% per-region (us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1) once dashboards show stable label coverage. After rollout, we will remove the compatibility recording rule and update remaining dashboards/alerts in follow-up PRs. Operational notes: If tier tagging is missing, the request is tagged tier=unknown and deployment_mode=unknown; alerts/dashboards should exclude unknown from SLO accounting (see migration note). This PR intentionally does not change SLO math; it only makes the tier dimension available and consistently propagated.
changed_areas: api-gateway/telemetry: tier classifier + metric label injection
api-gateway/request-context: add TierInfo to context + propagate to routing client
docs/internal: dashboard/query migration notes + rollout checklist
commit_summary: api-gateway: add TierClassifier (hosted vs dedicated) and expose in RequestContext
telemetry: tag SLI metrics with tier + deployment_mode; add unknown fallback
streaming: classify termination reasons and tag stream termination metric
routing-client: propagate tier fields over internal RPC metadata
prometheus: add temporary recording rule mapping legacy labels to tier/deployment_mode
docs: add dashboard/query migration notes + rollout steps
migration_notes: Dashboard/query changes: 1) Replace label filters {pool="dedicated"} or {account_tier="dedicated"} with {tier="dedicated"}. 2) Where dashboards previously inferred tier from route_name prefixes, switch to tier/deployment_mode; keep route_name only for drill-down. 3) For SLI accounting, exclude tier="unknown" until rollout reaches 100% in the region: e.g., sum(rate(api_gateway_request_total{tier!="unknown"}[5m])). 4) The compatibility recording rule sli:api_gateway_request_total:by_tier will exist for ~2 weeks to bridge old dashboards; after that, dashboards must query the source metrics directly with tier/deployment_mode. Known caveat: Dedicated requests that enter via older enterprise gateway pods without the feature flag will emit unknown; this is expected during phased rollout and should not page by itself.
review_conversation: Allison Grant: Can you confirm the SLI boundaries here? Specifically, are we tagging at the first point we consider "ingress" for SLO accounting (after auth + request validation), and are we excluding 4xx/429s from the same counter series or separate? I want to ensure we don’t accidentally count invalid requests against tier budgets.

Amara Diallo (author): Yes—metrics are emitted after auth/tenant resolution and request schema validation. We keep existing SLI semantics: 4xx and 429 are emitted but excluded by SLO queries (unchanged). This PR only adds tier/deployment_mode labels; it does not change the HTTP code classification logic. I added a note in the migration doc and a small comment in metrics.ts to make this explicit.

Thomas Baird: Please double check cardinality. Adding tier is fine, but deployment_mode might be redundant. Any chance this becomes a free-form value (e.g., VPC/onprem) later and we explode series count?

Amara Diallo (author): Good call. deployment_mode is an enum with a hard-coded allowlist in tier_classifier.ts (hosted_api|dedicated_pool|unknown). I added a unit test to ensure unrecognized values map to unknown, and the internal propagation uses the same enum type. Private/VPC will be handled later but will require explicit enum expansion + review.

Mina Haddad: Propagation into routing: do we preserve tier through fallback? Some of our fallback paths create a new context. If the routing client drops tier, downstream SLO accounting will be wrong.

Amara Diallo (author): We now attach TierInfo to RequestContext and pass it through the routing-client metadata. Routing can still override model/region, but the tier remains the original ingress tier. I also added a regression test in routing-client to ensure TierInfo is forwarded even when fallback_policy is set.
Logan Wright: Telemetry side: do we need to emit tier on traces too? It’d be useful to slice exemplars by tier in the tracing UI.

Amara Diallo (author): Already included—RequestContext attaches tier/deployment_mode as span attributes on the gateway root span. Downstream services that consume our context will inherit and can add to their spans. Not changing any sampling policies here.

Allison Grant: One more request: please add a short "unknown" handling note + recommended dashboard exclusion filter. We’ve had confusion before when partial rollouts made graphs look "better" due to missing labels.
Amara Diallo (author): Added to migration notes section (exclude tier=unknown during rollout) and called out in the PR description. Thanks.
release_notes: Internal: Gateway SLI metrics now include tier and deployment_mode labels to support tiered SLO/error budget dashboards. Dashboards should migrate to the new labels; see docs/observability/tiered-slos/migration-notes-ingress-tier-tags.md.
